wacc_rationale.notes: UNCHANGED on this refresh -- no evidence altering liquidity, concentration, key-person or execution risk emerged. NZ$37m-ish market cap, ~NZ$7k/day turnover (severe illiquidity, +2.0). Revenue ~100% NZ with an agriculture/dairy customer skew (+1.0). Founder-CEO holds 20.7% and has personally relocated to run the AU launch (+0.5). AU execution risk is primarily charged in the scenario flows and weights (bear 25%); only a residual +0.5 sits in the WACC to avoid charging the same risk twice (owner-fcf.md section 7f). ~20% of revenue is wholesale-rate-dependent rather than execution-dependent (+0.5). Zero debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 16% used for all three scenarios — per-scenario WACC differences would charge risk a third time.

base.narrative: UNCHANGED from the prior build: Australia gains a modest foothold: processing-fee growth accelerates from 10% to a 13% peak as AU adds customers off the Payday Super catalyst, then decays to 5% by FY2036 (revenue NZ$19.7m). Pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips to 8% in FY2027 on AU go-to-market spend, then ramps to a mature 28%. Capitalised-development capex tapers from 22% to 10% of revenue post platform build. Float interest steps down to ~NZ$1.45m as the OCR cycle bottoms, then grows slowly with the float. Cash tax is sheltered by the NZ$8.26m loss pool through most of the explicit window -- the corrected (lower) SBC path now leaves EBIT high enough that the pool exhausts mid-Y10, one year earlier than on the prior overstated-SBC basis, so Y10 carries a small cash tax charge (~13% effective) even before the terminal 28% normalisation. Only the SBC path changed on this refresh; all other assumptions unchanged.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (AU launched April 2026, 40 customers, pricing already ~20% below plan, management's own risk register flags ~60% partner-channel dependence). Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right simultaneously: partner-channel activation, Payday Super conversion, NZ platform migration without churn, and float interest stabilising. The SBC correction moves bear equity value from negative to marginally positive but does not change the underlying execution-risk judgment that sets these weights.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position >>100 means the price sits far beyond even the street (SBC-as-non-cash) ceiling of the base case: the market is not paying for either accounting basis of the current business at a 16% micro-cap discount rate — it is paying for bull-case Australian success at a much lower implied discount rate. The SBC correction raised both house and street IV materially (house +25.8% to 0.0539, street +12.2% to 0.0779) but did not close this gap because the correction improves the flows, not the multiple the market is applying.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

valuation_philosophy: This valuation deliberately reads as brutal against a NZ$0.23 price. PaySauce's FY2026 owner FCF is NEGATIVE even after the 2026-09-25 SBC correction reduced the deduction (from -0.96m on the overstated SBC basis to -0.72m corrected): reported profit exists only because 2.21m of development cost was capitalised, ~20% of revenue is wholesale-rate interest on other people's money (falling as the OCR eases), and the company is entering a multi-year Australian investment phase that its own commissioned research models as loss-making through FY2028. At a 16% NZD cost of equity — justified line-by-line by micro-cap illiquidity (~NZ$7k/day turnover), sector/country concentration, key-person and residual execution risk — even a bull case in which Australia broadly works (NZ$40m revenue, 32% margins by FY2036) is worth ~NZ$0.12. The current price therefore embeds both bull-case AU execution AND a discount rate this liquidity profile does not merit. The stock is an option on Australia, and the model prices the option honestly rather than capitalising the hope. The SBC correction genuinely improved the economics (weighted IV rose from $0.042 to $0.054, +28%; bear equity value flipped from negative to marginally positive) but did not close the gap to the market price, because the correction fixes the flows, not the multiple the market is paying.
dashboard_banner: Model approach: owner-FCF DCF with the revenue split into processing fees (grown) and float interest (rate-dependent, modelled flat-to-down — never extrapolated). Customer payroll float (NZ$45.2m) is excluded from cash; FY2017-18 shell years excluded from history; terminal value tax-normalised at 28%. The sanity check did NOT trip on overvaluation — the DCF sits far BELOW the market price: weighted IV NZ$0.054 vs NZ$0.23, because at a 16% micro-cap discount rate the market price can only be justified by bull-case Australian success. This is an option-on-Australia stock, not a cash-flow stock, at today's price.
